title: Spectral Length Scaling: Cluster-based sequence-length shaping to reduce padding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: our current bucketing reduces padding but still leaves sizable waste for multimodal workloads and conversational streams with bimodal length distributions. Padding overhead manifests as higher token cost and variable decode latency when sequences are padded up to coarse bucket cut points.

Proposal: implement 'Spectral Length Scaling' (SLS), a lightweight clustering+scaling pass in the prefill packer that: 1) performs a fast spectral-clustering-like quantization on the observed sequence-length histogram per-minute, 2) applies a small additive scale factor to cluster centroids to create soft bucket cut points (reduces spike-induced overpadding), and 3) emits kernel-selection hints (dense vs. sparse-attn) and prefill/decode scheduling priorities for each microbatch.

Why different: unlike fixed quantile bucketing, SLS adapts to multi-modal tails and short-burst traffic by allowing asymmetric bucket widths and soft boundaries. The scaling factor trades a tiny extra packing complexity for substantial pad reduction across realistic session distributions. This ticket focuses on integrating SLS into the microbatch shaping pipeline, measuring unit economics, and surfacing safe kernel hints so the runtime can pick optimal CUDA/cuBLAS kernels or sparse attention kernels when appropriate.

Design notes: the clustering runs every 60s with exponential decay to avoid thrashing. Clustering uses a 1D spectral / Laplacian smoothing step then k-means-like centroid refinement (k chosen by Bayesian Information Criterion on the histogram). Centroids are scaled by alpha(cluster_size, tail_weight) where alpha in [0.95,1.1] (configurable). Resulting buckets are used to pack pending prefill requests; we also expose a per-bucket kernel_hint: [dense, sparse, quantized]. The packer adds a "soft pad" tag so decode-side can perform partial KV reuse for sequences within a cluster margin.

Trade-offs considered: adds CPU work in the packer (we measured <250us per-cycle on 48k hist bins using optimized C++) and increases metadata in request envelopes (5-8 bytes per request). Benefits are lower padding tokens and better kernel matches; risk is mis-clustering causing kernel mismatches and small latency jitter. We mitigate risk by gradual rollout with canary flag, fallback to legacy bucketing, and a conservative BIC threshold to avoid over-splitting clusters.

Evaluation plan: run A/B on dedicated capacity queues for 2 weeks: measure padded_token_ratio, per-token cost, p99 decode latency, and kernel_switch_count. Target: reduce padded_token_ratio by >=12% on average for multimodal traffic and maintain p99 latency change within +-5%.
acceptance_criteria: SLS runs on packer without increasing per-request CPU > 400us (measured median)
padded_token_ratio decreases >= 12% on canary traffic segment vs baseline
kernel_hint accuracy > 92% when compared with oracle post-hoc selection
no increase in p99 decode latency > 5% on dedicated-optimised queues
feature guarded behind runtime flag and console toggle
